newsitem.title: YEMEN: Saudi interior minister in Yemen for border talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi interior minister in Yemen for border talks.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's interior minister said in Yemen on Monday he was confident the two neighbouring countries would reach an agreement to settle a 61-year border row, the official Yemeni news agency SABA said.

Prince Nayef bin Abdul-Aziz said on his arrival in the capital Sanaa that he was carrying a letter for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh dealing with bilateral issues, especially the border dispute.

"We are confident that through deep awareness of common interests and brotherly and national awareness of the two countries...we will, God willing, reach an agreement which will be accepted by both sides," he said.
An official told Reuters Prince Nayef was expected to meet Saleh within a few hours and leave Yemen on Tuesday.

Yemen, one of the region's poorest countries, and oil-rich Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the border dispute. A joint committee looking into border demarcation has met scores of times since then, but its work is moving at a snail's pace, diplomats say.

Yemen has hinted in recent months it might resort to international arbitration. The two countries had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before they signed the deal.
